citations.assessment: The Bavli recounts three separate disputes and introduces them in the order Africa, Egypt, Ishmael and Keturah. It explicitly dates the abandonment in the first two disputes to a sabbatical year.
Rashi reads a bent back from the dialogue with the sectarian. Attribution to advanced age is Heilprin’s wording.
The a fortiori argument explicitly turns on those who had never lived and those who had previously lived.
The midrash gives Gevia ben Kosem and has Canaanites rather than Africans as the name in the land dispute. The same section also recounts a threatened alteration of his forehead or hump.

notes.text: The Bavli gives the plain hedyot wording and does not introduce a priest in the offer. The same phrase recurs in the later disputes.
The Mishnah explicitly counts three priestly and twenty-one Levitical guard stations. This supports Heilprin’s objection to inferring priesthood from being a guard.

The headword has not been recovered in a checked direct Arukh witness. The digital Yuchasin reading cites Arukh under Gevia explicitly, and the exact name occurs in the direct Bereshit Rabbah parallel.
